FAULKNER BALDWIN AND OCHOA MEDICAL GROUP - DISCHARGE SUMMARY

Patient: Robles DOB: 08/01/1963 Sex: M MRN: 235169
Admit: 12/23/2022 Discharge: 01/05/2023

Principal diagnosis: Proteinuria
Secondary diagnoses: Epilepsy / seizure disorder, dental abscess, inguinal hernia s/p repair

Admitting diagnosis: Proteinuria with urine protein level of 85 mg/dL.
Secondary diagnoses on included epilepsy with a seizure disorder, with medication and a seizure-free period of 1.9 years, a dental abscess, and a history of inguinal hernia status post repair.

Hospital course: Mr. Robles was admitted on 12/23/2022 with a diagnosis of proteinuria. His urine protein level was noted at 85 mg/dL. He has a history of epilepsy, which has been controlled with carbamazepine, and he has been for approximately 1.9 years. Additionally, he presented with a dental abscess, for which he has been taking amoxicillin 500 mg. His past surgical history includes an inguinal hernia repair.

During his hospital stay, Mr. Robles underwent a series of diagnostic tests to evaluate the cause of his proteinuria. These tests included a complete blood count, comprehensive metabolic panel, and a urinalysis. The results were within normal limits except for the elevated protein in the urine. An ultrasound of the kidneys was performed, which showed no structural abnormalities. His blood pressure was recorded at 131/71 mmHg, and his weight was 104 pounds on his last visit on 11/09/2024. Previous weights were 116 pounds on 12/20/2023, and 117 pounds on 01/29/2023.

Mr. Robles' hospital course was uneventful. He was monitored for any signs of complications related to his proteinuria and other conditions. His vital signs remained stable throughout his stay. He was advised on lifestyle modifications to manage his proteinuria, including dietary changes and the importance of regular follow-up with his primary care physician.

Discharge medications: Mr. Robles was discharged on carbamazepine 200 mg twice daily for his seizure disorder and amoxicillin 500 mg three times a day for his dental abscess. He was instructed to complete the course of antibiotics as prescribed.

Social history: Mr. Robles is a current tobacco user, chewing several times a day, a habit he started on 03/11/2019. He consumes approximately one alcoholic drink per week.

Follow-up: Mr. Robles is to follow up with his primary care physician, Dr. Jorge Rivera, for further management of his proteinuria and to monitor his other chronic conditions. He was also advised to schedule an appointment with a de

ntist to address his dental abscess and with a surgeon to evaluate the status of his inguinal hernia repair.

Discharged to: Home in stable condition.
